data.label: Receive SIEM Alert
data.description: Start the workflow when the SIEM system triggers a security alert.
data.rationale: This is a deterministic event trigger from the SIEM system. No uncertainty handling, language understanding, or AI is needed. L0 is sufficient.
data.errorHandling: If the webhook payload is missing or invalid, reject the event, log a validation error, and emit a dead-letter event for manual review. Retry only on transient transport failures.

data.label: Triage Alert
data.description: Review the alert by checking severity, source IP reputation, and affected assets.
data.rationale: This can be implemented as deterministic rule evaluation and lookups against known severity mappings, IP reputation feeds, and asset inventory. I start at L0 and do not need ML unless the alert data is highly ambiguous; the description does not require that.
conditions: alert severity, source IP, and affected asset fields are present
data.errorHandling: If any lookup fails, retry with exponential backoff for transient API errors. If reputation or asset inventory is unavailable after retries, mark triage as partial and route to manual analyst review.

data.label: Assess Severity
data.description: Determine whether the alert is critical, moderate, or a likely false positive.
data.rationale: Severity classification can be handled with deterministic thresholds and rule-based logic based on alert attributes. I only move beyond L0 if the task requires probabilistic classification, but that is not explicit here.
data.errorHandling: If severity cannot be determined from the configured rules, default to escalated handling and flag the alert for analyst confirmation. Log the rule gap for tuning.

data.label: Isolate Endpoint
data.description: Immediately disconnect the affected endpoint from the network to contain a critical incident.
data.rationale: This is a direct deterministic response action through endpoint security controls or network management APIs. No AI or inference is needed.
data.errorHandling: If isolation fails, retry once immediately, then fall back to network containment via NAC/quarantine VLAN and raise a high-priority manual escalation.

data.label: Notify Security Team
data.description: Send an urgent PagerDuty notification to the security team about the critical alert.
data.rationale: Sending a PagerDuty notification is a straightforward API action with fixed message formatting and routing rules. This is purely deterministic orchestration.
data.errorHandling: If PagerDuty is unavailable, retry with exponential backoff and send a backup notification via email/Slack webhook. Record delivery status for audit.

data.label: Run Forensic Scan
data.description: Automate collection of logs, memory dumps, and network traffic captures from the affected environment.
data.rationale: This step coordinates multiple tool actions and likely requires dynamic environment-aware execution across endpoints and systems. I start at L0, but the need to orchestrate multiple collection tools and handle runtime variation justifies moving to L4. It is not L5 because this is still one orchestrating agent rather than multiple collaborating agents.
conditions: incident is confirmed or requires deep investigation
data.errorHandling: If one or more collection tasks fail, continue collecting the remaining artifacts and mark missing evidence. Retry transient collection failures up to 2 times; if still failing, attach the failure reason to the incident record.

data.label: Collect Logs
data.description: Gather relevant system, application, and security logs for investigation.
data.rationale: Log collection is a deterministic retrieval task from known sources. The step is rule-based and does not require language understanding or reasoning.
data.errorHandling: If a log source is temporarily unavailable, retry collection and continue with available sources. If access is denied, flag the source and proceed with the rest of the evidence.

data.label: Collect Memory Dumps
data.description: Capture memory dumps from the affected endpoint or host for forensic analysis.
data.rationale: Memory dump acquisition is a deterministic operational action. It involves executing a known capture procedure, not AI-based decision making.
conditions: endpoint is reachable and permissions allow acquisition
data.errorHandling: If memory capture fails due to process lock or permissions, retry once, then fall back to acquisition via EDR-assisted capture or note the limitation.

data.label: Collect Network Captures
data.description: Capture network traffic data relevant to the incident for later examination.
data.rationale: Packet capture is a deterministic data collection operation using known filters and endpoints. No ML or LLM capability is needed.
conditions: network path or sensor is available
data.errorHandling: If live capture is not possible, fall back to existing network sensor logs or firewall telemetry. Retry transient sensor failures with backoff.

data.label: Correlate Findings
data.description: Compare evidence across multiple data sources to identify the likely attack vector.
data.rationale: This requires combining heterogeneous evidence across logs, memory, and network data, likely using search, parsing, and analysis tools. I start at L0, but simple rules alone are insufficient because the step depends on dynamic evidence correlation and investigation logic. A single tool-augmented agent is appropriate, not multiple agents.
conditions: at least one evidence source collected
data.errorHandling: If correlation is inconclusive, iterate over additional search queries and enrich with threat intel lookups. If still ambiguous, produce a partial hypothesis set and flag for analyst validation.

data.label: Generate Incident Report
data.description: Create a report containing the incident timeline, impact assessment, and recommended remediation steps.
data.rationale: This step involves generating a narrative report from investigation findings. I start at L0, but the task requires language generation and summarization, which moves it to L3. No external tools are required if the inputs are already available.
data.errorHandling: If report generation fails, retry with the same structured input. If the output is incomplete, regenerate sections independently and preserve existing validated sections.

data.label: Update SIEM Rules
data.description: Tune SIEM detection rules to reduce recurrence of the identified false positive pattern.
data.rationale: Rule tuning can often be represented as deterministic edits, but identifying the correct false-positive pattern from historical alert data may require a narrow supervised model or statistical classifier. I start at L0, but because detection tuning involves variation across alert patterns, L1 is more appropriate than pure rules in this context.
data.errorHandling: Validate proposed rule changes against historical alerts before publishing. If validation indicates overfitting or regressions, do not deploy; instead queue the change for analyst approval.

data.label: Document False Positive
data.description: Record the false positive pattern and relevant context for future detection tuning.
data.rationale: Documentation requires generating a concise summary of the false positive pattern and context. I start at L0, but the need to compose human-readable documentation makes this an L3 language generation task.
data.errorHandling: If the documentation service is unavailable, queue the note for later publishing and retain a local draft. Ensure the pattern is still stored in the incident record.

message: The workflow now includes deterministic tool bindings, enriched conditions, parallel forensic collection, and explicit error/loop paths. Critical alerts isolate the endpoint and notify PagerDuty before running parallel evidence collection. False positives route to SIEM rule updates and documentation, with validation and fallback handling for API failures, partial evidence, and inconclusive correlation.

workflow.workflowBrief: When a security alert is triggered by the SIEM system, triage the alert by checking severity, source IP reputation, and affected assets. For critical alerts, immediately isolate the affected endpoint and notify the security team via PagerDuty. Run an automated forensic scan to collect logs, memory dumps, and network traffic captures. Correlate findings across multiple data sources to identify the attack vector. Generate an incident report with timeline, impact assessment, and recommended remediation steps. For false positives, update the SIEM rules and document the false positive pattern for future tuning.
